summary: Dropping a polymorph ring onto a sink reaches the implemented js/do.js:dosinkring path, but its RIN_POLYMORPH arm records note_unported("do.c polymorph_sink") and skips the entire C transformation. do.c:polymorph_sink consumes rn2(4), changes the sink into a fountain, throne, altar or room/grave, carries over the looted state where C does, sets altar or fountain fields, prints the transformation result and redraws the square. In this case C chooses an altar and consumes a second rn2(3); JavaScript leaves the terrain as a sink, causing the RNG mismatch at segment 0 step 37 and the screen/cursor mismatches at step 38. The whole missing do.c function is the source owner. C also calls it from fountain.c:dipsink, while the JavaScript sink-dipping path remains fail-closed in potion.js.

source.branch: At the hero square, do.c:polymorph_sink proceeds only when the terrain is SINK. do.c:dosinkring reaches it for a dropped RIN_POLYMORPH; fountain.c:dipsink reaches it for POT_POLYMORPH. Implement its complete guard, sink-state capture and clear, all four rn2(4) transformations, the altar alignment and Inhell branch, the room-to-grave attempt, terrain-specific message, and newsym call. The v14 case reaches outcome 2 (altar), with rn2(4)=2 followed by rn2(3)=1.
callers: C cmd.c drop command -> do.c:dodrop -> do.c:drop (713-780) -> dosinkring (497-661) -> polymorph_sink (582-585). At the examined commit, JS cmd.js:runDropCommand (3432-3437) -> do.js:dodrop (1303) -> internal drop (1405), which calls do.js:dosinkring (1040) for a ring on a sink; its RIN_POLYMORPH arm at do.js:1144-1149 currently records the missing call and skips it.

C potion.c:dodip (2321-2331) -> fountain.c:dipsink (716-745) -> polymorph_sink (582-585). At the examined commit JS potion.js dodip throws UnsupportedDipError for at_sink; fountain.js has no dipsink implementation, so this separate C caller is not wired in JavaScript yet.
dependencies: mkmaze.c:set_levltyp updates sink and fountain feature counts. The examined JS already imports js/terrain.js:set_levltyp, which performs that count update.

RNG rn2; Inhell and Align2amask; terrain and feature state fields typ, flags/looted, blessedftn and altarmask; and the defsyms explanation used in the transformation message. The examined JS already has rng, In_hell, Align2amask, terrain mutation, symbol and display/message facilities for these dependencies.

engrave.c:make_grave is missing from examined js/engrave.js. In polymorph_sink case 3, make_grave mutates terrain/engraving and can call get_rnd_text (including rn2); polymorph_sink immediately reads the resulting terrain type to choose its symbol and message. This dependency must be implemented or otherwise completed from source; skipping it would leave the whole-function port incomplete.

evidence: The assigned queue entry in .cache/v14-baseline-work-queue.json records remainingScreens=2, recordedSteps=40, manifest corpus SHA-256 a2a371fd7e9049f3f852a5af862930b3302d2facde5019077d00a04e860807e0, recording SHA-256 ca63f820be4d8aa1c05d2ae7f7bafd2cce9633ac1ca418fc3a6708580e7a6e0d, and evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260929225551-v14.json at de8f73ddf16241bca4e484fef2ab099b3f133a2d. That evaluation reports 38/40 screens, 38/40 cursors, and 2285/2287 RNG calls matched; its first mismatch is C rn2(4)=2 from polymorph_sink(do.c:416) at segment 0 step 37, followed by a screen and cursor mismatch at step 38.

The assigned scan .cache/synthetic-scans/v14/polymorph-ring-transforms-sink.json has no command refusal and records do.c polymorph_sink in JS unported state. Its first RNG divergence is the missing C rn2(4)=2 from do.c:416; the next screen differs at row 0, column 0, and its segment end remains input-boundary mismatched. challenges/manifests/v14.json sourceTraceEvidence identifies the two C calls at do.c:416 and :436.

At frozen source commit 3212f9f07c3fdf3f00c5c204885f51834f0b6448, js/do.js:1144-1149 handles RIN_POLYMORPH by calling note_unported("do.c polymorph_sink"), then continues with the unchanged sink terrain. The C caller at do.c:582-586 instead calls polymorph_sink before reading the resulting terrain. The full C definition at nethack-c/upstream/src/do.c:401-456 establishes the source scope: sink guard; save looted status and clear flags; rn2(4) switch for fountain, throne, altar or room/grave; outcome-specific feature fields; transformation/vanishing message; and newsym. The observed altar case consumes rn2(3) at do.c:436 after the first draw.

The C body also depends on engrave.c:make_grave for outcome 3, which may change terrain, add a headstone engraving and draw randomness for an epitaph. The JS implementation at the examined commit has make_engr_at/engr_at but no make_grave or get_rnd_text implementation; because polymorph_sink reads the terrain after this call, that dependency cannot be silently skipped. The other C caller, fountain.c:dipsink, is downstream of a JavaScript sink-dipping refusal in potion.js and is not the path reached by this challenge.
